newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso dips amid reviving industry demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso dips amid reviving industry demand.

text.p: Colombia's peso dipped 0.7 to 1,079.1 against the dollar amid heavy demand for greenbacks offset by banks shortening dollar positions, interbank traders said.

Speculation about the looming U.S. decision about whether to "certify" Colombia as a trustworthy ally in the drug war or blacklist it for a second consecutive year continued to fuel speculation in the market, interbank traders said.
The United States has threatened to clamp economic sanctions on Colombia if it were decertified again.
"Speculation continued today but there was much stronger demand from industry," one trader said.
He said rises were restrained because banks, which had built up long dollar positions as the greenback began to gain, moved to sell foreign currency to make up for peso shortfalls.
Traders reported operations worth a total $151 million. The peso hit an intraday high of 1,078.5 and sank to an intraday low of 1,083.
